question: does taking each swath-to-swath tie as the fitted intercept at across-track position zero, instead of the unweighted overlap median, remove the tile-extent dependence of the gen1 per-swath constants -- and what does it do to the DoD?

inputs.role: pipeline corrections actually shipped for this tile: grid geometry and the per-swath constants this run must reproduce before changing them
gen1 2008 cloud with PDAL CSF ground classification, cached by pipeline.difference_dem (ground_source='csf'), raw coordinates
pipeline corrections actually shipped for this tile: grid geometry and the per-swath constants this run must reproduce before changing them
gen1 2008 cloud with PDAL CSF ground classification, cached by pipeline.difference_dem (ground_source='csf'), raw coordinates
per-return gen1 CSF ground offsets to the gen2 surface, slope-normal mm, with the four registration terms and point_source_id / scan_angle per return
per-return gen1 CSF ground offsets to the gen2 surface, slope-normal mm, with the four registration terms and point_source_id / scan_angle per return
the DoD in use: gen2 at the cover-dependent percentile minus gen1's registered median, m, + = elevation rose
gen2 gridded ground, the DoD reference surface, m

params.name: reproduction tolerance (vertical)
params.why: the gate on whether the re-derived shipped ties ARE the shipped ties. 1 mm is the coarsest level at which a reproduction failure could still matter here: it is a sixth of the smallest tie change measured below and an eighth of the smallest tile-to-tile disagreement being explained. The achieved values are printed per tile and per axis; it excludes no data.

params.name: gauge swath
params.why: chosen by a stated rule on measured quantities, not by taste: of the lines BOTH tiles carry (135, 136, 137, 138), the one whose worst |mean scan angle| across the two tiles is smallest -- the line both tiles sample most symmetrically about nadir. Its effect is measured below and is a LEVEL shift only (tests/test_coreg.py proves the gauge changes no swath-to-swath difference), so it excludes no data and moves no gradient.

columns.tile: derived-product directory / cached cloud the numbers come from
columns.pair: adjacent flight-line pair A-B (point_source_id), A < B
columns.cells: overlap grid cells the pairwise tie used
columns.dz_med: pairwise vertical tie from the shipped overlap median, mm (+ = line B must be raised onto line A)
columns.dz_int: the same tie from the across-track intercept at dtan = 0, mm
columns.delta: dz_int - dz_med, mm: what the extent-dependence was worth on that link
columns.c_mm: across-track slope fitted with the intercept, mm per unit tangent
columns.mean_dtan: mean of tan(scan_A) - tan(scan_B) over the pair's overlap cells in this tile: the across-track position the shipped tie averages at
columns.pred: -c_mm * mean_dtan, mm: the shift the ramp predicts for this link, against which delta is the measured value
columns.returns: in-grid gen1 CSF ground returns of that line
columns.scan_mean: mean scan angle of that line's in-grid returns, deg (signed)
columns.scan_sd: standard deviation of that line's scan angle, deg
columns.scan_p5: 5th percentile of that line's scan angle, deg
columns.scan_p95: 95th percentile of that line's scan angle, deg
columns.asym: |mean scan| of the line, deg: 0 means the tile samples it symmetrically about nadir, large means the tile only ever sees it off to one side
columns.dz_old: per-swath constant from the shipped tie, re-referenced as stated, mm
columns.dz_new: per-swath constant from the intercept tie, re-referenced as stated, mm
columns.elba_old: elba's constant for that swath, shipped tie, re-referenced to 135, mm
columns.ext_old: elbaext's constant for the same swath, shipped tie, ref 135, mm
columns.dis_old: elba_old - ext_old: the tile-to-tile disagreement, shipped tie, mm
columns.elba_new: elba's constant, intercept tie, re-referenced to 135, mm
columns.ext_new: elbaext's constant, intercept tie, ref 135, mm
columns.dis_new: elba_new - ext_new: the same disagreement, intercept tie, mm
columns.removed: dis_old - dis_new, mm, and as a percentage of dis_old
columns.gauge: which flight line the network is pinned to, and with which tie
columns.level: point-count-weighted mean vertical shift of the gen1 cloud under that gauge, mm: the level the tile's whole DoD inherits
columns.raster: DoD raster file this run wrote
columns.md_mm: median change in the DoD against the shipped raster, mm
columns.lo_mm: most negative change in the DoD, mm
columns.hi_mm: most positive change in the DoD, mm
columns.subset: which shared flight lines the summary is taken over
columns.spread_old: max - min of the tile-to-tile disagreement over those lines, shipped tie, mm (independent of the gauge)
columns.spread_new: the same spread with the intercept tie, mm
columns.rms_old: RMS of the disagreement after removing its mean over those lines, shipped tie, mm (independent of the gauge)
columns.rms_new: the same RMS with the intercept tie, mm

headline: intercept tie changes elba's constants by +0.0, +5.9, +5.8, +5.1 mm; the elba/elbaext disagreement goes -8.02, -9.66, -17.41 -> -2.04, -2.11, -9.81 mm
